newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Fire hits PDVSA Curacao refinery - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Fire hits PDVSA Curacao refinery - spokesman.

text.p: A "big fire" hit one distillation unit of the 310,000 barrel per day (bpd) Curacao refinery operated by Petroleos de Venezuela on Thursday morning, cutting production from a normal 180,000 bpd to 60,000 bpd, a spokesman for the refinery said.
Crude distillation unit number three, which normally runs at 130,000 bpd, was disabled by the fire, but some production was continuing in the other two atmospheric towers at the plant, he added.
Workers had yet to inspect the damage caused by the fire, but it had only affected a small part of the distillation tower and he said it could be 80 percent returned to service soon.

"We still have to go and see what the damage is before we know what time it will take to repair. The unit consists of two columns and we think we can take 80 percent of it into operation sooner," he said.
"Unit number two was planned to go into revision today, but we will keep it in operation now," he added.
The Curacao refinery is rented by Petroleos de Venezuela on 20 year contract and is a major supplier of refined oil products for the United States market.
